details:
**Ron DeSantis**
The Republican governor of Florida since 2019, governing from the capital Tallahassee. He became a national conservative figure by banning school mask mandates during COVID-19, rejecting the College Board's AP African American Studies pilot course, and fighting "woke" policies; critics also mocked him for allegedly wearing height-boosting boots.

**Champlain Towers South collapse**
The partial collapse of a beachfront condominium in Surfside, in Miami-Dade County, in June 2021, which killed 98 people. A 2018 report by Morabito Consultants had warned of major structural damage, possibly made worse by saltwater corrosion. Surfside mayor Charles Burkett and Miami-Dade mayor Daniella Levine Cava were prominent in the response, and Levine Cava ordered an audit of older high-rises.

**Andrew Gillum**
The Democratic former mayor of Tallahassee who narrowly lost the 2018 governor's race to DeSantis. Donald Trump called him a "thief" during the campaign.

**Charlie Crist and Nikki Fried**
Crist, a former Republican governor who became a Democrat, criticized long voting lines under Governor Rick Scott in 2012. As a congressman, he beat Agriculture Commissioner Nikki Fried in the 2022 Democratic gubernatorial primary and then lost to DeSantis in a landslide.

**"Don't Say Gay" law and the Disney feud**
The 2022 Parental Rights in Education Act, called "Don't Say Gay" by opponents, restricted classroom instruction on sexual orientation and gender identity. After Disney CEO Bob Chapek pledged to help repeal it, DeSantis retaliated by moving to strip the special self-governing tax status of Disney's Reedy Creek Improvement District.

**Martha's Vineyard migrant flights**
In September 2022, DeSantis's administration chartered flights that took about 50 mostly Venezuelan migrants from Texas to the wealthy Massachusetts island of Martha's Vineyard. The stunt protested federal immigration policy and drew lawsuits and accusations that the migrants were deceived.

**15-week abortion ban**
A law DeSantis signed in April 2022 that banned most abortions after 15 weeks of pregnancy, months before the Supreme Court's Dobbs decision. Florida later adopted a stricter six-week ban.

**Marco Rubio and Rick Scott**
Florida's two Republican U.S. senators for most of the late 2010s and early 2020s. Rubio served in the Senate from 2011 until he became Donald Trump's Secretary of State in 2025, and Scott was Florida's governor from 2011 to 2019 before joining the Senate.

**Social media deplatforming law (SB 7072)**
A 2021 Florida law that would have penalized social media companies for banning political candidates. The tech industry groups NetChoice and CCIA sued to block it, arguing that it violated the First Amendment and Section 230. Around the same time, Florida also passed a ban on transgender girls in girls' school sports.

**Parkland aftermath (Scott Israel and Kyle Kashuv)**
After the 2018 Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School shooting in Parkland, DeSantis suspended Broward County Sheriff Scott Israel days into his term over the department's response. Kyle Kashuv, a conservative gun-rights activist who survived the shooting, had his Harvard admission rescinded after racist messages he wrote earlier surfaced.

**Palm Beach: Mar-a-Lago and the Jeffrey Epstein plea deal**
Donald Trump's Palm Beach resort Mar-a-Lago was called the "Winter White House," and he hosted Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe there in April 2018. In 2008, Alex Acosta, then U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of Florida, approved a lenient plea deal for Palm Beach financier Jeffrey Epstein, which forced Acosta to resign as Trump's Labor Secretary in 2019.

**2012 election and PolitiFact**
Florida was the closest state in the 2012 presidential election, and the Republican National Convention was held in Tampa. PolitiFact, founded by the St. Petersburg (now Tampa Bay) Times, rates false claims as "Pants on Fire" and named a Romney ad about Jeep moving production to China its 2012 "Lie of the Year." Florida politicians in clues from that era include DNC chair Debbie Wasserman Schultz and Tea Party congressman Allen West, who claimed 78 to 81 House Democrats were communists.

**Maxwell Frost and Byron Donalds**
Frost, a Democrat from the Orlando area elected in 2022, became the first member of Gen Z in Congress. Donalds is a Black Republican congressman from southwest Florida and a member of the House Freedom Caucus.

**The Perfect Neighbor**
An Oscar-nominated documentary built largely from police body-camera footage about the 2023 killing of Ajike "AJ" Owens, a Black mother in Ocala. Her white neighbor Susan Lorincz shot her through a closed door after a dispute over children playing, and Lorincz was later convicted of manslaughter.

**Citrus greening (HLB)**
Huanglongbing, a bacterial disease spread by the Asian citrus psyllid insect, which makes fruit green, bitter, and misshapen. It has devastated Florida's once-dominant orange industry and caused a steep fall in production.
